title: Team 7
subtitle: Quantum sensing for water-quality changes
body: A continuous-variable simulation of a dissolved-salt proxy
28% lower modeled total error in a controlled 16-tap pilot
NYUAD Hackathon • Research prototype • October 2026
notes: Working team name confirmed by user. Final Arabic/English name, confirmed student/mentor roster with affiliations and contact details, team photo and team logo remain to be supplied. No identity or affiliation is invented. Result is 27.92% total RMSE reduction against coherent probes, at 10 nW/node, 1 s and assumed 50 µK common temperature residual. Source: results/summary.json. The supplied template says its presentation/demo guidance is for the in-person event; October ideation has no presentation. This deck is prepared for reuse and discussion.

title: The problem and proposed solution
subtitle: UN monitoring evidence and an operator use-case hypothesis
body: UN 2025: poorest regions supplied 60,000 of ~2 million reporting measurements.
EPA: online monitoring supports treatment decisions and event investigation.
Proposed user: an operator investigating mean composition changes across taps.
Our contribution: water-proxy CV simulation with loss, drift and fair baselines.
notes: UN SDG Report 2025, Goal 6: https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/report/2025/Goal-06/ reports approximately two million measurements used for reporting, 60,000 from poorest regions. These are monitoring data, not all worldwide measurements. WHO 2023 fact sheet, 2022 data: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/drinking-water . EPA online monitoring: https://www.epa.gov/waterresilience/online-water-quality-monitoring-resources . These sources establish importance and monitoring use cases, not a quantum bottleneck or salt-based pathogen detection. Operator need for this dose and sensitivity is an assumption. 16 taps is a design assumption: four binary splitter stages and Ns=1.6 below the 2.025 photons/mode cap. Not optimal or deployment-derived. Guo et al. demonstrated four nodes: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.09408 . Start with one/four measured taps. 100 m links, 10 nW/tap and 50 microkelvin residual are assumptions. Our contribution integrates existing CV theory with a NaCl proxy, losses, technical noise and decision analysis. No research-priority claim. docs/DESIGN_DECISIONS.md.

title: How the simulation runs
subtitle: Classical CPU computation of a proposed quantum optical sensor
body: Inputs: default.json assumptions and a CSV of 64 distinct coordinates.
Python 3.12: NumPy covariance, SciPy probability, pandas data, Matplotlib plots.
Compute phase sensitivity and loss, then mean variance plus drift and calibration.
Outputs: RMSE, detection probabilities, synthetic time traces and ten figures.
notes: Implementation evidence: src/model.py, src/run.py, src/validate.py, src/practical_comparisons.py and requirements.txt. Local Python 3.12.14 CPU execution. NumPy 2.3.5 arrays, covariance, seeded Gaussian draws; SciPy 1.18.1 constants and normal CDF, root solve in comparison helper; pandas 2.2.3 CSV processing; Matplotlib 3.11.2 PNG/SVG figures. Python unittest runs 13 internal model checks. Inputs: config/default.json and data/site_geometry.csv. Chemical concentrations in the trace are synthetic; coordinates only from supplied USGS-labelled file. Compute phase slope, loss, covariance, w^T Sigma w, add thermal/calibration variance, then threshold tests. Most RMSE curves are analytic. Monte Carlo: 100,000 null and alternative draws per strategy. A separate synthetic OU time trace has response lag. Seed 2601006. Outputs: results/summary.json, CSV, feasibility.npz, ten figures. Run bash src/reproduce.sh in project root with prepared .venv. No quantum SDK, circuit execution, ML training or quantum hardware. JavaScript/Node artifact-tool creates PPTX; Python creates offline HTML; Playwright prints PDF. Authoring tools are separate from the scientific simulator. Details: docs/SIMULATION.md.

title: 28% lower total error in the pilot
subtitle: 16 taps • 100 m links • 10 nW/node • 1 s • 50 µK common residual
body: Coherent 0.0921 → distributed 0.0664 mg/kg total RMSE
16.6% lower RMSE than independent squeezing; same launched probe photons
notes:
Quantum justification: 20%. This is a prediction for a proposed controlled instrument, not a measured water sensor. Optical RMSE .079619 vs .047583; total precision gain 1.387×. The ambitious common temperature residual is an engineering assumption. Probe photon accounting includes squeezed photons deducted from carrier power, but excludes pump and local oscillator energy.
results/summary.json pilot16. No measured-field accuracy claim. Common residual 50 microkelvin is an ambitious compensated bench target.

title: Ideal scaling has resource conditions
subtitle: Lossless reference • Growing total squeezing • No practical source cap
body: Fitted RMS slope: −0.953 distributed versus −0.500 coherent
Loss and a finite source cap remove the asymptotic exponent advantage
notes:
Fit uses M=33–64. Total squeezing Ns=.1M grows with M; fixed per-node carrier power also grows total probe energy. Ideal panel removes loss, phase jitter, technical errors and the 10 dB cap. It is not a forecast of field scaling. See figures/05_resource_accounting.png for fixed-total budgets and docs/MODEL.md. Consistent with qualified CV theory; no independent experimental proof.
Computed by src/model.py and results/summary.json. Per-node squeezed budget 0.1 photon/mode, total Ns=0.1 M; equal launched bright-plus-squeezed photon budgets. S4 asymptotic displacement model.

title: Regional gain shrinks to 1.11×
subtitle: 64 distinct supplied coordinates • Assumed routes • Optimized coherent baseline
body: Mean transmission 0.371; longer links replace squeezing with vacuum noise
Total RMSE: optimized coherent 0.0729 → distributed 0.0655 mg/kg
notes:
Source geometry is USGS-labelled input from the draft; no independent provenance or available fiber is established. Nearest 64 unique coordinates to assumed LA hub 34.05,-118.24; lengths 1.3×great-circle distances. Straight distances 3.5245–16.6434 km, mean routed length16.3847km. Fiber anchor .18dB/km, Corning AN2008. Changing M changes the sampled population. Coherent allocation F_i proportional to 1/sqrt(eta_i), relaxing individual power cap at fixed total photons. Source Ns capped2.025 photons/mode.
data/site_geometry.csv derives coordinates only from draft. 8889 records reduce to 7704 coordinate pairs; nearest64 selected. As M changes, sampled population changes, so this is not a sensor-reduction claim for one fixed spatial target.

title: Temperature can erase the benefit
subtitle: Common drift does not average away across more sensors
body: 10 mK residual → about 9.137 mg/kg error for either strategy
~28 nW/tap coherent matches the 10 nW quantum result under the same drift.
notes:
Water thermo-optic anchor https://opg.optica.org/abstract.cfm?uri=sensors-2012-STu1F.3 . At the NaCl slope, 1mK appears as .916mg/kg. 50µK controlled and10mK stress residuals are assumptions; neither is a manufacturer Gaussian noise claim. OU correlation60s. YSI temperature accuracy±.01C is contextual, not statistical conversion. Power sweep1nW–70µW in Figure10 independently tests a stronger classical alternative.
S10 reports dn/dT≈−1.485e−4 RIU/K at1550nm. The exact coefficient depends on temperature/composition. 0.05 mK and10 mK are assumed stochastic residuals, not manufacturer statistical specifications. Derived same-model comparison: results/practical_comparisons.json.

title: A matched detection comparison
subtitle: 0.15 mg/kg step • 16 taps • 1 s • 1% false alarm per decision
body: Detection probability rises from 24.3% to 47.3% under the model
1% at 1 Hz means 36 expected flagged windows/hour: an alarm policy is still needed
notes:
Analytic Gaussian ROC validated by100000 null and100000 alternative independent draws per strategy. This is marginal repeated-experiment validation, not an operational sequential detector. Temperature correlations, non-Gaussian tails and response lag require time-series validation. No regulatory threshold or guaranteed detection is implied. Measurable SDG6-related monitoring proxy, not measured environmental impact.
results/detection.csv. Independent Monte Carlo marginal windows, not independent samples of the OU trace. Assumes Gaussian moments including squeeze-angle jitter. Decision threshold is not regulatory. Bonferroni alpha=0.05/3600 bounds hourly familywise false-alarm probability at5% without independence.

title: Demo: continuous monitoring
subtitle: Synthetic unequal arrivals • Shared drift • Explicit sensor lag
body: The quantum mean is cleaner; neither method removes lag or identifies a chemical
Demo: compare truth, filtered response and observations in the figure gallery
notes:
Offline demo: open figures/index.html and Figure07. Explain 16 different arrivals90–135s, mean amplitude.35mg/kg with±25% variation, rise25s, response10s,1s sampling. Shared thermal and calibration realization for both methods. Show Figure08 to change the discussion to loss/temperature limits, then Figure10 to challenge the low-power premise. No live hardware is represented. Stationary RMSE excludes transient lag bias.
results/time_trace.csv. Synthetic changes, not observed water data. Independent optical noise, common OU realization, seed2601006. Optical noise advantage concerns the aggregate; local contrasts do not receive the same benefit.

title: Measured anchors / design assumptions
subtitle: Sources establish a mechanism; the complete water device remains unvalidated
body: Measured anchors: NaCl index slope, telecom squeezing, fiber attenuation, water dn/dT.
Design targets: 10 µm interaction, 10 dB cap, 1 MHz mode rate, 50 µK residual.
Supplied sensing experiment: RF air measurement, not slow water calibration.
16 taps: assumed four-stage split, below source cap. Published CV precedent: four.
notes: NaCl: Saunders https://doi.org/10.1364/AO.55.000947 ; squeezing Mehmet https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.3737 ; fiber https://www.corning.com/media/worldwide/coc/documents/Fiber/application-notes/AN2008.pdf ; thermo-optic Kim https://opg.optica.org/abstract.cfm?uri=sensors-2012-STu1F.3 . Supplied Dowran https://doi.org/10.1364/OPTICA.5.000628 reports795nm199kHz air sensitivities8.6/6.8/5.5e-10RIU/sqrtHz; not transferable to1s1550nm water. Supplied Pooser/Lawrie PDF is supporting information of a separate paper. QML https://doi.org/10.3390/quantum8030060 ; matched RBF remains strong. Complete sources and each config parameter in docs/PROJECT_REPORT.md AppendixA. 16 taps is a design assumption: four binary splitter stages and Ns=1.6 below the 2.025 photons/mode cap. Not optimal or deployment-derived. Guo et al. demonstrated four nodes: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.09408 . Start with one/four measured taps. 100 m links, 10 nW/tap and 50 microkelvin residual are assumptions. Our contribution integrates existing CV theory with a NaCl proxy, losses, technical noise and decision analysis. No research-priority claim. docs/DESIGN_DECISIONS.md.

title: Business sustainability and scalability
subtitle: Start with a controlled plant laboratory
body: Alternative: conventional conductivity or a stronger coherent optical probe.
Possible path: a paid research pilot, then a calibrated monitoring module.
Scale only after surveyed routes, measured drift and useful detection justify cost.
No verified customer, pricing, partner commitment or net energy saving yet.
notes: Sustainability/scalability15%. Business model is a hypothesis; avoid unsupported market size or demand claims. Seek water operator and optical lab partnership, with a budget based on equipment quotations. Local calibration and infrastructure review required for UAE/Arab-region and other deployments. Data access, incident privacy, maintenance and confirmatory sampling are future product requirements. YSI EXO contextual comparator https://www.ysi.com/product/id-599870/exo-conductivity--temperature-smart-sensor ; accuracy bounds are not a fair ratio to simulated differential RMSE.

title: Next steps and decision gates
subtitle: A measured advantage must survive practical alternatives
body: 1  Calibrate one water cell: slope, bias, temperature response and transmission.
2  Test four taps with blind salt changes and matched coherent/squeezed budgets.
3  Measure full energy, false alarms and detection delay before a 16-tap pilot.
Proceed only if useful detection improves under an operator-relevant constraint.
notes: Proposed research stages, not completed work or promised dates. Full electrical meter includes pump, local oscillator, locking, electronics and classical compute. Acceptance proposal: RMSE ratio confidence interval below1 with prespecified budgets, then time-based false-alarm target agreed with operator. Need evidence10nW dose constraint matters; if higher-power coherent or conventional sensing achieves same goal with lower burden, prefer it. Organizer confirmation needed that quantum sensing satisfies the rubric’s quantum-computing focus.

title: Three measurable claims
subtitle: Simulation evidence today • Operational outcomes to measure next
body: Estimation: 27.92% lower total RMSE at matched launched probe photons.
Water monitoring: 24.3% → 47.3% detection of the specified salt-proxy step.
Resource use: 160 nJ probe energy per pilot window for both strategies.
Liters saved, wall-plug energy and field advantage remain unmeasured.
notes: Required closing three claims from judging guidance. All pilot claims use16nodes,10nW/node,1s,50µK common residual. Detection uses.15mg/kg increase and1% false alarm per decision. Optical energy160nJ is equal resources, not measured sustainability improvement. Algorithm is estimator accuracy, not quantum computational runtime. Next KPI: total joules per validated useful detection at matched coverage, false-alarm rate and response time. Results do not prove/disprove literature: conditional model consistency only.

title: Evidence and judge questions
subtitle: Appendix • Full derivation, ten experiments and source register in the report
body: Why quantum? Correlated readouts improve the specified mean under a dose budget.
Practical alternative: ~28 nW/tap coherent matches 10 nW/tap distributed RMSE.
What is proven? Internal model checks; no hardware or field claim.
What is missing? Chemical specificity, low-frequency stability, total cost and energy.
